proseChanges.summary: **Access hardening — an owner changes a teammate's sign-in only where that workspace is the account's only one:** a teammate's password, second factors and recovery codes belong to the account, not to one workspace, but before this release an owner of any workspace the account belonged to could issue it a password-reset link or reset its two-factor sign-in, which changed how the account signs in for its other workspaces too. Now: (1) an owner's password-reset link for a teammate is issued only while that workspace holds the account's sole membership and the account does not administer the installation, otherwise it is refused with `409`, and the link names that workspace; (2) accepting such a link checks the same rule again in the write itself, so a link whose account has since joined another workspace is refused (`409`, "This reset link no longer applies") and spends nothing; (3) an owner's two-factor reset for a teammate (their factors and recovery codes removed, their sessions ended) is refused with `409` for an account that also belongs to another workspace or administers the installation, and its three deletions carry the same condition; (4) the reset link an account holder requests by email (`forgot-password`) now belongs to the account and names no workspace, so it is not tied to this rule. An account that also belongs to another workspace changes its own sign-in. Invitation links are unchanged: the shared token check that invitation acceptance uses carries the reset rule for reset links only. An unused reset link issued by v0.4.20 or earlier for an account that belongs to more than one workspace, or administers the installation, is refused after the upgrade: request a new one by email. No migration and no data step: deploy the new Worker. **Known limit — the roster corner for teammates erased by v0.4.19 or earlier is wider than the v0.4.20 notes said:** a Business that keeps listing an erased teammate by real address without a member id gets the same re-creation one revision later, and the first such revision keeps their name and address in the stored Business settings; the code fix is a Base round (gr-base-roster-corner-1). A Business that sends member ids is fenced. **Migrations:** No migrations since v0.4.20. v0.4.21 adds no migration file, so a v0.4.20 installation's migration ledger stays unchanged.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.20 is the last published release, with migrations through 323.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.21 adds access hardening for owner-issued password resets and two-factor resets of teammates, widens the known roster corner for teammates erased by v0.4.19 or earlier, and adds no migration since v0.4.20. Published upgrade baselines are v0.4.20 and v0.4.19.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.20 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.107. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. v0.4.21 adds no migration, so a v0.4.20 installation applies nothing before the new Worker serves traffic. Earlier installations apply every missing published migration once, in filename order, BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic (a v0.4.19 or v0.4.18 installation applies exactly 322_contact_address_lookup.sql, then 323_business_retired.sql; v0.4.17 also needs 321_legacy_import_files.sql, then `node scripts/legacy-import/upgrade.mjs --project <legacy project id>` once per workspace imported from legacy, as the v0.4.18 notes describe; v0.4.16 also needs 320_legacy_import_work_repair.sql); retain each migration's buyer steps. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Live-provider qualification and owner cutover remain separate.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1 first; apply once after 323_business_retired.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive and index-only: creates seven indexes (conversation_tags_conversation on conversation_tags (conversation_id, project_id, tag_id); conversation_outbox_undelivered on conversation_outbox (conversation_id, project_id) for undelivered rows only; conversation_outbox_conversation on conversation_outbox (conversation_id); conversation_outbox_project on conversation_outbox (project_id); workflow_events_due on workflow_events (state, coalesce(next_attempt_at, 0)); workflow_events_pending_ids on workflow_events (state, id); workflow_events_lease on workflow_events (state, lease_token)), so the every-minute scheduler, outbox delivery, a live connection's replay and a conversation's tag reads search the work that is due instead of walking every outbox row, pending workflow event or tag of the database; no row changes, no trigger is recreated, and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a large imported workspace each index builds in under a second.

Back up D1 first; apply once after 324_scheduler_outbox_reads.sql, before serving the updated Worker. Additive only: creates one index on knowledge_documents (knowledge_documents_version_url on (version_id, url)), so the knowledge reference policy's check that an older crawl version's page still has a current twin at the same URL searches an index instead of walking every page of the published version; no row changes and nothing is read, sent or queued. On a crawled site of a few thousand pages it applies in under a second.
